learning_outcomes.text: Students taking Thermal Engineering II must understand the fundamentals of the operation of thermal machines and engines at an energy level, and from there, be able to solve the problems that an Engineer usually faces in the exercise of their profession.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for concretizing them and their clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for teamwork and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of the Thermodynamic Behavior of Volumetric Internal Combustion Engines with Termograf
Analysis of the Thermodynamic Behavior of Gas Turbine Engines with Termograf
Analysis of the Thermodynamic Behavior of Vapor Turbine Engines with Termograf
Disassembly and Assembly of an Internal Combustion Engine
Obtaining the characteristic curves of an Internal Combustion Engine
Obtaining the indicated cycle in a cylinder of an Internal Combustion Engine
Determination of the operating parameters of a Gas Turbine
Determination of the operating parameters of a compression refrigeration system
assessment_rules: All exercises in exams have the same value unless otherwise specified. An exercise is correct when the correct result is obtained; if incorrect due to minor errors, it is considered correct if not absurd or if recognized by the student. Chained questions are evaluated independently unless a previous part is absurd and not recognized. Grades are on a scale of 0-10: Fail (< 5), Pass (5-6.9), Notable (7-8.9), Outstanding (9-10).
